title: Time to Access and vascular complications after venous access using standard of care needle vs. ultrasound needle in electrophysiological ablation procedures
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate whether ultrasound-guided groin puncture using a special ultrasound needle during catheter ablation leads to a reduction in groin complications compared to the standard puncture needle, and to compare the time required for successful puncture (skin penetration to successful sheath insertion) and any pain in the groin after the intervention.

interventions.name: Use of the standard puncture needle set for ultrasound-guided puncture of the femoral vein for access during interventional cardiac ablation treatment
Use of a special puncture needle (PAJUNK) that is more visible in ultrasound for ultrasound-guided puncture of the femoral vein for access in the context of interventional cardiac ablation treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients capable of giving consent after providing written consent
Exclusion criteria:
lack of capacity to consent, or withdrawal of consent to participate in the study
